In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of action of antimicrobial peptides and their interaction with the bacterial membrane.

the characterization of antimicrobial peptide-membrane interactions and their effect on the membrane structure and stability in order to better understand the mechanisms of action of antimicrobial peptides and to develop new strategies for the rational design of new antimicrobial agents.
the characterization of the physico-chemistry of the interaction of antimicrobial peptides with bacterial membranes and the correlation of these findings with their antimicrobial activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of CL is a key element for the antimicrobial activity of myxinidins and that the N-terminal tryptophan plays a key role for the antimicrobial effect of the peptide.
the antimicrobial activity of myxinidins depends on the membrane composition and on the presence of CL.
the presence of the tryptophan at the N- terminus of WMR and the additional positive charges play a crucial role in the antimicrobial activity of this peptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WMR is a more promising peptide than myxinidin for future therapeutic applications.

the presence of the N-terminal tryptophan and the additional four positive charges in WMR, compared with myxinidine, are responsible for a better interaction of WMR with P. aeruginosamembrane bilayer and for a greater antimicrobial activity.
the antimicrobial activity of a given peptide depends on the physicochemical properties of the membrane, which in turn are related to the lipid composition of the bacterial cell membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of CL in the bacterial membrane is a crucial factor in the WMR activity.

the interaction of the peptides with the membrane depends on the membrane composition, and that the presence of anionic cardiolipin can be exploited to enhance the antimicrobial activity of antimicrobial peptides.
the interaction with membranes is crucial for the antimicrobial activity of the peptide, and the presence of cardolipin in the membrane plays a key role for the activity of WMR.
